subject: College Avenue Green Line Station Proposal
overview: Medford, Tufts University, the MBTA, and the Cummings Foundation announced a partnership to construct a new Green Line station and academic building at College Avenue. The proposal includes $550,000 in direct payments to the city and several infrastructure improvements funded by the private partners.

items.title: Welcome and Project Overview
items.summary: Mayor McGlynn opened the press conference to unveil a collaborative proposal for the College Avenue station involving the city, Tufts, the MBTA, and Cummings Property. He noted the project aims to improve pedestrian safety and neighborhood access while providing new community spaces.

items.title: Tufts University Academic Building Proposal
items.summary: President Monaco detailed plans for a new academic building above the station that will include community meeting space, first-floor retail, and a public footbridge to the upper campus. He confirmed the building will exclude wet labs and student housing and pledged annual payments to the city.

items.title: MBTA Partnership and Financial Commitments
items.summary: Interim General Manager DiPaola stated that Tufts has committed to funding all improvements and maintenance for the station plaza, ensuring the project has no negative impact on the MBTA budget. The agreement includes a 99-year lease for the university to use the air rights above the public right-of-way.

items.title: Cummings Foundation Support
items.summary: Bill Cummings discussed his foundation's history of local philanthropy and expressed support for the station project as a continuation of efforts to revitalize Medford neighborhoods.

items.title: Community Benefits and Public Process
items.summary: Mayor McGlynn outlined a $500,000 community fund payment schedule from Tufts and an additional $50,000 for city signage and peace garden maintenance. He concluded by announcing that the project will now enter a formal public review and permitting process.
